key_insight: Disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion promote dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings, while higher humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray parameters to minimize coating porosity can improve long-term corrosion resistance on Q235 carbon steel.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Characterize droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and sliding wear under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear involves Si3N4–water tribochemistry, so results may not transfer directly to other counterface materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
